summary: Answered the two registered gaps and tested the trigger's scope. Gap 1 (the generalized decided-log read) is resolved from the two receipts themselves: with two inflated reporters the leader's decision at index 7 pushed the re-synchronized replicas' decided index past the StopSign index so their decided-log read from 0 kept the StopSign alone (receipt 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 events 19, 20 against 22, 23; reproduced in receipt 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63), while with one inflated reporter the decided index stayed at 6 with accepted 7 so the same read returned an empty list (event 35 against 19, with nodes 2 and 3 untouched at 36, 37). Gap 2 is answered partly by source reasoning and left open: with the resume point equal to the sender's decided index the snapshot branch of create_log_sync is not entered even when snapshots are enabled, and when entered it derives sync_idx from get_decided_idx_without_stopsign (excluding the StopSign), so the inflation is not specific to NoSnapshot entries, but no snapshot-enabled run has been executed and no execution has yet sampled a leader inflated in its own accepted index. Because the same resume point also arises on the ordinary re-synchronization path (a re-promising follower whose accepted round equals the leader's own promise round, and a candidate leader whose own decided index becomes sync_idx in the follower's Promise), the explanation now records that broader reach and a successor experiment is submitted whose newterm case cuts off node 2 and lets node 1 take the lead in a new term with only node 3's promise; the baseline comparisons require every replica to report the StopSign as decided with a six-element decided read before the change, and the result comparisons require the re-synchronized follower (node 3) to keep its endpoint, its decided index bound, its StopSign at index 5 and its six-element decided read, with the new leader and the cut-off node staying consistent. Incomplete: that execution, the leader-side inflation witness, a snapshot-enabled run, loss-triggered re-synchronization, and the internal accepted-index vector behind the phantom decision.
